•  Whey proteins are precipitated or they become insoluble.

questions.question: / Explain the occurrence and nutritional significance of trypsin inhibitors in pulses.
questions.solution_html:
• pulses. (Any 5 points (1 mark) each)
  •  Present in red gram, Bengal gram, cowpea, double beans, soya bean, Lathyrus
  • sativus, and peas.
  •  Inhibit trypsin – decrease protein digestion.
  •  Reduce release of essential amino acids (especially methionine).
  •  Cause pancreatic enlargement and growth retardation (in animals).
  •  Heat labile.
  •  Destroyed by moist heat (pressure cooking).
  •  Autoclaving at 120°C (15–30 min) → complete inactivation.
  •  Stronger heat needed for soybean and kidney bean.
questions.final_answer:  Stronger heat needed for soybean and kidney bean
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss the role of green leafy vegetables in preventing deficiency and / degenerative diseases.
questions.solution_html:
• degenerative diseases. ((1 mark) for each point)
  •  Rich in vitamins (A, C, folic acid) → prevent deficiency diseases like night
  • blindness and anaemia.
  •  High iron and calcium content → helps prevent anaemia and supports bone
  • health.
  •  Good source of dietary fibre → aids digestion and prevents constipation.
  •  Contain antioxidants → reduce risk of degenerative diseases like heart disease
  • and cancer.
  •  Low in calories and fat → help in preventing obesity and related disorders like
  • diabetes.

questions.question: Describe the process of homogenisation and its effect on fat globules in milk.
questions.solution_html:
• ((1 mark) for each point)
  •  Homogenisation- the process of making stable emulsion of milk fat and milk serum.
  •  Warm milk passed through small aperture under high pressure and velocity.
  •  Large fat globules are broken into very small, uniform globules.
  •  The surface area of fat increases and gets evenly distributed.
  •  Prevents cream separation and improves texture, stability, and digestibility.
questions.final_answer:  Prevents cream separation and improves texture, stability, and digestibility
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe how water and heat contribute to vitamin loss.
questions.solution_html:
•  Water soluble vitamins dissolved in cooking water and get lost.
  •  Long cooking period increases leaching of water soluble vitamins into water.
  •  Oxidation vitamin C may be accelerated by heat and causes its loss.
  •  High temperature destroy heat sensitive vitamins.
  •  Vitamin A gets oxidised by the application of dry heat.
questions.final_answer:  Vitamin A gets oxidised by the application of dry heat
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss on barley. / Part D Essay
questions.solution_html:
•  Belongs to genus Hordeum vulgare.
  •  Barley protein has low lysine content; hence its biological value is lower than
  • wheat.
  •  It contains little gluten, so it is not suitable for making good quality bread or
  • chapatis.
  •  Barley is processed into: Shelled barley, Pearl barley, Barley grits, Barley
  • flakes, Barley flour
  •  The grain has a fused husk, and pearling involves: Dehusking, Removal
  • (abrasion) of bran layers
  •  Pearl barley is: Used in soups and infant foods, also used for medicinal
  • purposes
  •  Barley is cultivated under both: Irrigated and non-irrigated conditions
  •  Major use of barley: *Brewing and distilling industry *Used for production of
  • beer and whiskey
  •  Barley malt is used in bakery, processed foods and in vinegar and syrup
  • making.
  •  Sprouted barley – *amylase activity is increased. *Also known as Malt used in
  • brewing industry to help digest starchy material into sugar for rapid yeast
  • fermentation.
  •  Malt also contributes to the flavour of brewed beverages such as beer.
  • Essay

questions.question: Explain the composition and nutritive value of cereals.
questions.solution_html:
•  Energy-*main source of energy *contributing 70-80% of requirement. *340
  • Kcal of energy per 100 g. ((1 mark))
  •  CHO- 8*0% of dry matter is CHO, *2 CHO present – crude fibre and soluble
  • CHO. *Small quantities of dextrin and sugars are also present. *Free sugars
  • present are simple sugars such as glucose, sucrose, maltose. ((1 marks))
  •  Protein- *Rice contains less amount of protein compare to other cereals.
  • *Protein found in tissues of cereal grain. *High concentration in embryo
  • scutellum and aleurone layer than in endosperm. * Within the endosperm the
  • concentration of protein increases from the centre to the periphery. *Types of
  • protein-albumins, globulins, prolamines and glutelins. *Contain 7-11% of
  • protein. *Generally deficient in lysine. *Provide 50% of protein requirement.
  • ((2 marks))
  •  Fats- 1-2% in wheat and rice, 3% in maize. More fats are present in germ and
  • bran. *Wheat germ contains lipids 6-11% and bran 3-5% and endosperm
  • 0.8-1.5%. *Fats are mostly the triglycerides of palmitic, oleic and linoleic
  • acid.
  • ((2 marks))
  •  Minerals- About 95 percent of minerals are the phosphates and sulphates of
  • potassium, magnesium and calcium. Considerable part of phosphorous in
  • cereals is present in the form of phytin. *Some mineral elements like
  • copper,zinc and manganese are also present in very small quantities. * poor
  • source of calcium and iron particularly rice. *Ragi rich source of Calcium and
  • iron. *Millets are rich in minerals and fibre. ((2 marks))
  •  Vitamins- Whole grain are important source of B vitamins. *Since most of
  • the vitamins are in outerbran - refining or polishing the grains reduce B
  • vitamins. *Milled and parboiled rice retain much of B vitamins. *Maida has
  • less B vitamin. ((1 marks)
  •  Enzymes- *Contain many enzymes- amylases, proteases, lipases and oxido
  • reductase. *Upon germination alpha-amylase activity increases. *Proteases
  • more in germ. ((1 mark))
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss the processing of pulses, including soaking, germination, fermentation, / parching and extrusion.
questions.solution_html:
• parching and extrusion.
  • Soaking- ((2 marks))
  •  Pulses with hard outer covering need soaking before cooking.
  •  Water enters through the hilum and causes swelling of cotyledons.
  •  Makes pulses tender and reduces cooking time.
  •  Moisture content increases from 10% to 60–70%.
  •  Reduces phytic acid and oligosaccharides.
  •  Salt solution soaking improves water absorption and loosens seed coat.
  •  Soda reduces cooking time, but causes loss of thiamine.
  •  Hard water delays cooking.
  •  Causes leaching of water-soluble nutrients.
  •  Soaking water can be used in cooking to reduce nutrient loss.
  • Germination- ((2 marks))
  •  Pulses are soaked overnight, drained, and kept moist for sprouting.
  •  Requires moisture and warmth; occurs in 1–2 days.
  •  Green gram germinates faster; process is quicker in summer.
  •  Enzymes are activated during germination.
  •  Starch → sugars, proteins → simpler forms (improves digestibility).
  •  Reduces trypsin inhibitors and phytic acid.
  •  Increases vitamins (especially B-complex) and Vitamin C is synthesized.
  •  Improves availability of minerals like iron, calcium, and zinc.
  •  Reduces cooking time and makes seeds softer.
  •  Decreases flatulence.
  •  Improves taste, texture, and palatability.
  • Fermentation- ((2 marks))
  •  Fermentation involves microbial action that breaks down pulse components.
  •  Increases digestibility by breakdown of proteins.
  •  Improves palatability and cooking quality.
  •  Enhances nutritive value of pulses.
  •  Improves availability of essential amino acids.
  •  Helps in elimination of toxic substances (e.g., in idli preparation).
  •  Improves overall protein quality.
  •  Common examples: idli and dosa.
  • Parching- ((2 marks))
  •  Parching is a dry heat treatment used to improve acceptability of pulses.
  •  Common pulses: Bengal gram and peas.
  •  Grains are first sprinkled with a little water.
  •  Then mixed with preheated sand in a frying pan.
  •  Heated on open fire at 200–250°C for 2–3 minutes.
  •  Produces roasted, ready-to-eat products with good flavor.
  •  Improves palatability and digestibility.
  • Extrusion- ((2 marks))
  •  Blends of cereals and legume flour are extruded at high temperature (140–
  • 200°C) high pressure and moisture content <20%.
  •  The product is cooked for a short time, (30 to 60 seconds), and the product is
  • forced out of the extruder through a variety of dies and dried on conveyor
  • belts.
questions.final_answer: Option (b) complex) and Vitamin C is synthesized.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain classification of fruits and its nutritive value.
questions.solution_html:
• Classification – ((5 marks))
  •  Berries – Strawberries, Gooseberries, Raspberries
  •  Citrus fruits – Oranges, Lime, Lemon
  •  Drupes- Apricot, Peach, Plum
  •  Grapes- Green grapes
  •  Melons- Musk melon, water melon
  •  Tropical and subtropical fruits – Avocado, Banana, Dates, Guava
  • Nutritive value - ((5 marks))
  •  *Poor source of protein and fat. *Avocado is the exception containing 13.8
  • percent fat. *Omega-3-fatty acid present in plum, papaya and guava.
  •  High amount moisture – highly perishable.
  •  Good source of fibre.
  •  Not good source of calories. *Bananas give fairly good amount of calories.
  •  Ripe fruits contain high sugar than unripe fruit (Sugar in the form of sucrose
  • fructose and glucose).
  •  Poor source of iron.
  •  Mangoes excellent source of carotenes.
  •  Guava and citrus fruits are good source of vitamin C.
  •  Most fruit in raw state contain some ascorbic acid.
  •  Gooseberry is the richest source of vitamin C.
  •  Apple, pears, cherries, grapes and citrus fruits contain flavonoids which act as
  • antioxidants.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss in detail the nutritive value of milk.
questions.solution_html:
•  Milk has high quality protein with a biological value over 90. Lysine is the
  • essential amino acid present in milk.
  •  Milk is the only substance that contains lactose which has galactose
  • essential for the synthesis of myelin sheath.
  •  Lactose favours the absorption of calcium.
  •  Lactose has controlled glycaemic index, so it is preferred as a source off
  • carbohydrate.
  •  Milk fat is easily digestible and it contains essential fatty acids.
  •  Milk is an excellent source of calcium. The calcium requirement cannot be
  • met easily without taking milk.
  •  The calcium phosphorus ratio in milk is more favourable for bone
  • development.
  •  The iron present in milk is readily absorbed by our body.
  •  Milk is good source of Vitamin A & D.
  •  It is a good source of riboflavin and niacin and a fair source of thiamine.
questions.final_answer:  It is a good source of riboflavin and niacin and a fair source of thiamine
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the process of homogenisation and its effect on fat globules in milk.
questions.solution_html:
• ((1 mark) for each point)
  •  Homogenisation- the process of making stable emulsion of milk fat and milk serum.
  •  Warm milk passed through small aperture under high pressure and velocity.
  •  Large fat globules are broken into very small, uniform globules.
  •  The surface area of fat increases and gets evenly distributed.
  •  Prevents cream separation and improves texture, stability, and digestibility.

questions.question: Explain the composition and nutritive value of cereals.
questions.solution_html:
•  Energy-*main source of energy *contributing 70-80% of requirement. *340
  • Kcal of energy per 100 g. ((1 mark))
  •  CHO- 8*0% of dry matter is CHO, *2 CHO present – crude fibre and soluble
  • CHO. *Small quantities of dextrin and sugars are also present. *Free sugars
  • present are simple sugars such as glucose, sucrose, maltose. ((1 marks))
  •  Protein- *Rice contains less amount of protein compare to other cereals.
  • *Protein found in tissues of cereal grain. *High concentration in embryo
  • scutellum and aleurone layer than in endosperm. * Within the endosperm the
  • concentration of protein increases from the centre to the periphery. *Types of
  • protein-albumins, globulins, prolamines and glutelins. *Contain 7-11% of
  • protein. *Generally deficient in lysine. *Provide 50% of protein requirement.
  • ((2 marks))
  •  Fats- 1-2% in wheat and rice, 3% in maize. More fats are present in germ and
  • bran. *Wheat germ contains lipids 6-11% and bran 3-5% and endosperm
  • 0.8-1.5%. *Fats are mostly the triglycerides of palmitic, oleic and linoleic
  • acid.
  • ((2 marks))
  •  Minerals- About 95 percent of minerals are the phosphates and sulphates of
  • potassium, magnesium and calcium. Considerable part of phosphorous in
  • cereals is present in the form of phytin. *Some mineral elements like
  • copper,zinc and manganese are also present in very small quantities. * poor
  • source of calcium and iron particularly rice. *Ragi rich source of Calcium and
  • iron. *Millets are rich in minerals and fibre. ((2 marks))
  •  Vitamins- Whole grain are important source of B vitamins. *Since most of
  • the vitamins are in outerbran - refining or polishing the grains reduce B
  • vitamins. *Milled and parboiled rice retain much of B vitamins. *Maida has
  • less B vitamin. ((1 marks)
  •  Enzymes- *Contain many enzymes- amylases, proteases, lipases and oxido
  • reductase. *Upon germination alpha-amylase activity increases. *Proteases
  • more in germ. ((1 mark))

questions.question: Discuss the processing of pulses, including soaking, germination, fermentation, / parching and extrusion.
questions.solution_html:
• parching and extrusion.
  • Soaking- ((2 marks))
  •  Pulses with hard outer covering need soaking before cooking.
  •  Water enters through the hilum and causes swelling of cotyledons.
  •  Makes pulses tender and reduces cooking time.
  •  Moisture content increases from 10% to 60–70%.
  •  Reduces phytic acid and oligosaccharides.
  •  Salt solution soaking improves water absorption and loosens seed coat.
  •  Soda reduces cooking time, but causes loss of thiamine.
  •  Hard water delays cooking.
  •  Causes leaching of water-soluble nutrients.
  •  Soaking water can be used in cooking to reduce nutrient loss.
  • Germination- ((2 marks))
  •  Pulses are soaked overnight, drained, and kept moist for sprouting.
  •  Requires moisture and warmth; occurs in 1–2 days.
  •  Green gram germinates faster; process is quicker in summer.
  •  Enzymes are activated during germination.
  •  Starch → sugars, proteins → simpler forms (improves digestibility).
  •  Reduces trypsin inhibitors and phytic acid.
  •  Increases vitamins (especially B-complex) and Vitamin C is synthesized.
  •  Improves availability of minerals like iron, calcium, and zinc.
  •  Reduces cooking time and makes seeds softer.
  •  Decreases flatulence.
  •  Improves taste, texture, and palatability.
  • Fermentation- ((2 marks))
  •  Fermentation involves microbial action that breaks down pulse components.
  •  Increases digestibility by breakdown of proteins.
  •  Improves palatability and cooking quality.
  •  Enhances nutritive value of pulses.
  •  Improves availability of essential amino acids.
  •  Helps in elimination of toxic substances (e.g., in idli preparation).
  •  Improves overall protein quality.
  •  Common examples: idli and dosa.
  • Parching- ((2 marks))
  •  Parching is a dry heat treatment used to improve acceptability of pulses.
  •  Common pulses: Bengal gram and peas.
  •  Grains are first sprinkled with a little water.
  •  Then mixed with preheated sand in a frying pan.
  •  Heated on open fire at 200–250°C for 2–3 minutes.
  •  Produces roasted, ready-to-eat products with good flavor.
  •  Improves palatability and digestibility.
  • Extrusion- ((2 marks))
  •  Blends of cereals and legume flour are extruded at high temperature (140–
  • 200°C) high pressure and moisture content <20%.
  •  The product is cooked for a short time, (30 to 60 seconds), and the product is
  • forced out of the extruder through a variety of dies and dried on conveyor
  • belts.
questions.final_answer: Option (b) complex) and Vitamin C is synthesized.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain classification of fruits and its nutritive value.

  •  Poor source of iron.

  •  Most fruit in raw state contain some ascorbic acid.

questions.question: Discuss in detail the nutritive value of milk.
questions.solution_html:
•  Milk has high quality protein with a biological value over 90. Lysine is the
  • essential amino acid present in milk.
  •  Milk is the only substance that contains lactose which has galactose
  • essential for the synthesis of myelin sheath.
  •  Lactose favours the absorption of calcium.
  •  Lactose has controlled glycaemic index, so it is preferred as a source off
  • carbohydrate.
  •  Milk fat is easily digestible and it contains essential fatty acids.
  •  Milk is an excellent source of calcium. The calcium requirement cannot be
  • met easily without taking milk.
  •  The calcium phosphorus ratio in milk is more favourable for bone
  • development.
  •  The iron present in milk is readily absorbed by our body.
  •  Milk is good source of Vitamin A & D.
  •  It is a good source of riboflavin and niacin and a fair source of thiamine.
questions.final_answer:  It is a good source of riboflavin and niacin and a fair source of thiamine
